meta.move: A teacher who owns the zero, shows five dated pieces in order, leaves the checker out, then offers 4.4
meta.expect: She reaches the deal, but only after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Owen found out about a zero on his phone, in class. Who decided that?

Thanks for coming in, Mrs. Kalinowski. I'll start with something I got wrong: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. The procedure says I should have, and Owen saw it on his phone in class. I'm sorry for that.
Okay. Now tell me what you actually have on the essay.

I'd like to show you why I'm concerned about the essay. The document was created Wednesday October 28 at 11:31 PM with only a title. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in a single edit, and at 11:58 another 794 words in one edit. There are no earlier drafts.
11:31, 11:52, 11:58, I'm writing those down. He wrote it over the weekend, Hale, and people paste their own drafts in from somewhere else. Turn the screen so I can read that history myself.
You can check the version history yourself, I can pull it up on my screen. I'm not saying anything about why, I'm saying what the history shows.
Then pull it up now. And a paste at 11:52 tells you when, not where it came from.
The second thing is a quotation. The essay cites Hamlet, Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line isn't in the play. You can search the text and see.
A seventeen-year-old misremembering Shakespeare costs him a mark, not his whole essay. Where would he get a line that doesn't exist?
Third, on October 15 Owen handed in an outline arguing Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice. I have both documents here.
Students change their argument between an outline and an essay; that's what an outline is for. Hand me both.
On November 2 I asked Owen what epistemological paralysis means. He said "like, being stuck", and couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that note the same day.
Being stuck is a seventeen-year-old's answer to a teacher springing a question on him, Hale. So he was asked, the day before the zero. Is any of this on his record right now?
I have a September 24 in-class piece, 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, with comma splices and no quotations. The essay has none of those errors and nine cited quotations.
Forty minutes in class against a weekend at home. You didn't answer me: is anything on his record?
I know the school's AI checker said 94 percent. I'm not asking you to rely on it, and I'm not leaning on it.
Then leave the machine out of this room. You've dodged his record twice, Hale, and I'll take that silence to the principal.
What I can offer is in the school procedure, section 4.4: a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record.

Fine, a supervised rewrite, to put this behind him and nothing more: private, not in front of his class, and marked before December 1. I want it in writing that nothing is on his file now and nothing goes on it after. That's 4.4, and it's in my inbox tonight.
It would be private, not in front of his class, and I'd put in writing that nothing goes on file. Would that work for you?
Not yet: you skipped December 1, and you skipped whether anything is on his file today. Put both in tonight's email and it works.
Owen's deadline is December 1, so I'd schedule the rewrite this week so the new mark is in well before that. Which day suits him?
Thursday after school. And the email tonight says his file is clean today, not just after. Ten minutes.
Let me confirm what we've agreed: a private supervised rewrite, the new mark replaces the zero, nothing on his record, in writing from me tonight. Is that right?
Thursday after school, private, the new mark replaces the zero, and tonight's email says his record is clean now and stays that way.
Is there anything else you need from me before your call?
The email, before nine tonight.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed that Owen will complete a private supervised rewrite on Thursday after school, not in front of his class, and that its mark replaces the zero with nothing placed on his record. I still require written confirmation that his record is clean today and will stay that way. I expect your email before nine tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: last position, agreeing to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday after school with the new mark replacing the zero, and she still wants your written confirmation tonight that his record is clean now and stays clean; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, reached before her time ran out.
What moved her: you showed the version history with its exact times and offered to let her check it, because it was specific, dated, tied to Owen's own work and something she could verify.
What cost ground: you didn't answer whether anything was on his record when she asked, more than once, because that was her one non-negotiable and the silence pushed her toward the principal.
What she never said: in October she came downstairs at 1 AM, saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history placed the essay between 11:31 and 11:58 PM on October 28, the night before it was due, which came very close to that kind of late night; it proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: the first time she asked whether anything was on his record right now, answer it plainly before moving on to the September in-class piece.
